history.summary: Sreekanteswaram Temple is a Shiva temple near the North Fort in Thiruvananthapuram, under the Travancore Devaswom Board. Per legend, an old sweeper woman of the Pazhaya (old) Sreekanteswaram Temple discovered a swayambhu Shiva lingam when her pot bled while resting under a tree; the king then built this new temple at the spot. The older Pazhaya Sreekanteswaram Temple at Puthenchantha is regarded as the original abode of the deity. The principal deity is Shiva as Sreekanteswara (Gowri Shankara - Parvati is considered ever-present, and the main sanctum is circular); sub-shrines include Krishna, Ganesha, Murugan, Ayyappan, Hanuman, Nagaraja and Parashakti. Note: CSV lists 'Sreekanteswaram Temple' - this file covers the main Sreekanteswaram Mahadeva Temple; do not confuse with the Pazhaya (old) Sreekanteswaram Temple nearby.

town_description: Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) is the capital city of Kerala on the state's southwest coast. It is home to the famous Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple, about 1 km from Sreekanteswaram, and the historic Fort area of the erstwhile Travancore kingdom. The city is a major rail and air gateway for southern Kerala.
